title: BINI, SB19 earn first Grammy nods
summary: P-pop groups BINI and SB19 earned their first Grammy nominations, while Filipino-American artists Bruno Mars and Olivia Rodrigo bagged nods in the top categories of the 2027 Grammy Awards.

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am

P-pop royalties BINI and SB19 have made history as the first Filipino groups to receive Grammy nominations. BINI’s ‘Unang Kilig’ and SB19’s ‘Visa’ are among the six nominees in the newly introduced Best Asian Pop Music Performance category at the 69th Grammy Awards scheduled for Feb. 7, 2027.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — P-pop groups BINI and SB19 earned their first Grammy nominations, while Filipino-American artists Bruno Mars and Olivia Rodrigo bagged nods in the top categories of the 2027 Grammy Awards.
During the nomination announcement held Monday evening, BINI’s “Unang Kilig” and SB19’s “Visa” were among the songs included in the inaugural Best Asian Pop Music Performance category.

After exploring genres, BINI went back to their bubblegum roots with “Unang Kilig,” written and produced by Jeremy G, which talks about the feeling of uncertainty and excitement in the first stages of romance.
“A historic moment for OPM (Original Pilipino Music), for Filipino music and for everyone who believes in them,” BINI said in a post.
“The girls are making history, and we couldn’t be prouder! Thank you to everyone who continues to support us,” they added.

On the other hand, Visa, written by Pablo and produced along with his brother Joshua Daniel Nase, draws inspiration from the group’s experience of the obstacles they have to just get their visa and perform abroad.
“From the Philippines to the world, thank you for believing in SB19 and standing with us as we carry Filipino music to the global stage!” SB19 said in a post.
As the agency’s ambassadors, the Department of Tourism (DOT) congratulated both groups’ new feats on the global stage.

“From rocking the historic stages of ‘Coachella’ and ‘Lollapalooza’ to earning recognition on the world’s biggest music stage, our country’s tourism ambassadors continue to prove that P-pop is a global force to be reckoned with,” the DOT said.
“The world is listening, and Filipino music is shining brighter than ever!” it added.

Other nominees in the Best Asian Pop Music Performance category include Sunset Kiss by the Japanese group Babymetal featuring Polyphia, Yes by Japanese singer Lisa and K-pop songs 404 (New Era) by KiiiKii and Bang Bang by Ive.

The Recording Academy said the Best Asian Pop Music Performance award aims to honor “artistic excellence in Asian pop music performances originating from or widely recognized within Asian markets, including but not limited to K-pop, J-pop and C-pop.”
However, the category drew flak from several music critics, stressing that it is boxing Asian acts instead of recognizing them alongside other global artists.

The criticism echoed when K-pop boy group BTS announced that they would not submit in this year’s awarding ceremony with their supposed comeback album “Arirang” after all of their members completed their mandatory military service.
Meanwhile, Filipino-American artists Olivia Rodrigo and Bruno Mars swept the pop and general field categories, making them some of the most nominated artists in this year’s awarding ceremony.
Bruno’s The Romantic and Olivia’s You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love bagged the Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album nominations.
Olivia’s The Cure was nominated in both Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance.
I Just Might by Bruno was nominated for Record of the Year, while Risk It All bagged nods for Song of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance.
Rodrigo’s “What’s Wrong with Me,” along with Robert Smith, was nominated for Best Rock Performance and Best Rock Song.
